papers.title: Tensor Recovery with Heterogeneous Mode Structures
papers.abstract: Tensor recovery methods often impose a common structural assumption across modes, even when different modes may exhibit distinct forms of regularity. We propose a unified convex framework that treats each mode according to its structure. Smoothly varying modes form an indexing domain and are handled by local kernel weighting, whereas retained modes may receive low-rank, group-sparse, graph-Laplacian, or autoregressive regularization in distinct and potentially overlapping combinations. The framework also covers ordinary tensor recovery without local smoothing. A consensus HM-ADMM algorithm separates the active penalties into tractable proximal and linear-system updates. For the population-quadratic estimator, we derive deterministic oracle inequalities and high-probability bounds under independent trace regression. The bounds disentangle stochastic error, rank and support complexity, smoothing bias, and quadratic mismatch. They also identify when quadratic penalties sharpen the Frobenius-error bound. For regular smooth domains, the theory characterizes the bias-variance trade-off and yields an optimal bandwidth order, with a specialization to uniform tensor completion. Simulations and two applications illustrate the gains from matching regularization to mode-specific structure, especially under severe undersampling.

papers.title: Infinity-Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Principal Component Analysis: Exact Reformulation, Finite-Sample Guarantee, and Efficient Algorithm
papers.abstract: Principal component analysis (PCA) is a fundamental and ubiquitous technique for dimension reduction and representation learning, yet its empirical formulation remains vulnerable to distributional uncertainty. While distributionally robust optimization (DRO) offers a natural remedy, existing order-2 Wasserstein models of PCA either preserve the nominal PCA subspace or lack an exact reformulation. This paper demonstrates how the infinity-Wasserstein distance can reconcile these two desirable properties. For the resulting DRO model of PCA, we derive an exact finite-dimensional reformulation and explicitly identify a worst-case distribution attaining the inner maximum. Crucially, the reformulated objective retains samplewise residual information beyond the empirical covariance matrix, revealing a mechanism through which distributional robustness can reshape the learned principal subspace. Under the mild assumption that the true distribution has a finite fourth moment, we further establish a uniform finite-sample performance guarantee for the proposed model. An iteratively reweighted majorization-minimization algorithm is also developed to solve the resulting nonconvex and nonsmooth optimization problem, with a rigorous analysis of its convergence properties. Numerical experiments substantiate the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithm and the practical effectiveness of the infinity-Wasserstein model in downstream applications.

papers.title: Model-Averaged Shrinkage Estimation of the Spectral Density Using Welch's Method
papers.abstract: We propose a shrinkage estimator of the spectral density based on a three-level hierarchical model. papers.title: Treatment Policy Design in the Presence of Measurement Error
papers.abstract: In many applications, treatments are assigned based on unit features, leading to personalized treatment policies. Treatment policies are then derived by comparing the null value of the CATE to these bounds. papers.title: Neural-network-powered new-physics searches by predictive goodness of fit
papers.abstract: Model-independent searches for new physics test whether data agree with a Reference model with unknown nuisance parameters. papers.title: Adaptive experiments with observational data: Efficient experimental design and asymptotic time-uniform inference for long-term treatment effects

papers.title: What Should an Experiment Measure? Combining a Short-Term Experiment with Confounded Observational Data to Identify Long-Term Treatment Effects

papers.title: What Environment Invariance Identifies: Minimal Invariant Sets in Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces

papers.title: Bayesian sequential decision-making for adaptive early warning of bridge failure risk
papers.abstract: As a critical functionality of structural health monitoring (SHM) systems, early warning of increased bridge failure risk is essential for structural safety. Through pre-posterior analysis over predicted future observations, the warning threshold is optimized by minimizing the expected total cost, which explicitly balances structural failure risks against warning response costs. The framework was verified via two bridge case studies covering typical scenarios that lead to increased structural failure risk, including steel truss member fracture and stay cable rupture. papers.title: Identification of Poisson processes through a one-dimensional projection
papers.abstract: We study the identification of stationary Poisson processes in Euclidean space through a single one-dimensional projection. Given a point process and a straight line, each point is retained independently with a probability given by a Gaussian function of its distance to the line; the retained points are projected onto the line. If the process is Poisson, the projection is again Poisson. What a single projection reveals depends on the sign of the second factorial cumulant, which is also the sign of the two-point correlations. Under a Palm domination condition, which holds for positively associated processes, the cumulant is nonnegative. Using a Chen-Stein argument we show that when the cumulant of the projection vanishes, the process is Poisson. Consequently, a single projection identifies non-Poissonianity. The same result holds under negative association. When the cumulant changes sign, a random projection detects a nonzero cumulant with probability one. We propose a test whose rejection region is computed by Monte Carlo. The test, together with a spacings-based variant for repulsive alternatives, rejects determinantal, shot-noise and other classical processes. When applied to lunar impact craters, the test rejects the Poisson hypothesis for craters with diameter below 30 km and does not reject it for craters above 45 km.

papers.title: Quantifying and calibrating precision gain from covariate adjustment in clinical trials with binary endpoints
papers.abstract: Covariate adjustment is widely used in randomized clinical trials to improve estimation and inference of treatment effects. papers.title: Spurious Information in Large Markets: Random Matrix Laws for Entropy, Mutual Information and the Value of Information
papers.abstract: Entropy, Kullback-Leibler divergence and mutual information have become standard currencies for measuring how much one set of financial variables reveals about another. Under independence its law is that of a product of Beta variables. In the proportional regime it grows linearly with an order-one variance. Spurious information increases strictly whenever uninformative coordinates are added.
